title: OpenMRS createGlobalStore usage in patient chart

answers.question: If `createGlobalStore` in the OpenMRS frontend framework (openmrs-esm-core) changed its behaviour, which code in the patient chart app (openmrs-esm-patient-chart) uses it and could be affected?

paragraphs.text: Three places in the patient chart call `createGlobalStore` directly; everything else is downstream of them.

**The declaration that would change**
`createGlobalStore` in `openmrs-esm-core` [1]. Its observable behaviour is: name-uniqueness via the module-level `availableStores` registry [2], returning the existing store and erroring on a second *active* creation, reactivating an inactive store by resetting its state [3], and the `storageType` argument choosing plain `zustand` vs `persist`+`sessionStorage` [4]. Note there are also mock versions with a narrower signature [5].
**Direct call sites in the patient chart**

| Store name | Call site | Behaviour it relies on |
|---|---|---|
| `order-basket` | `orderBasketStore` [6] | module-scope singleton, state reset by `_resetOrderBasketStore` [7] |
| `patient-chart-global-store` | `patientChartStore` [8] | singleton shared across the chart app |
| `ampath-form-state` | `store` in the Angular form-entry app [9] | `subscribe` + `getState`/`setState` only |

*Order basket — `order-basket`*
- `useOrderBasket` reads/writes via `useStoreWithActions(orderBasketStore, …)` and returns `orders`, `setOrders`, `clearOrders` [10]; its actions merge state immutably [11] and `clearOrders` calls `orderBasketStore.setState` with an updater [12]. Any change to singleton identity or to merge/replace semantics hits this.
- `getOrdersPayloadFromOrderBasket` and the second consumer at line 163 read `orderBasketStore.getState()` directly, so a change in initialization or state replacement changes the posted order payload packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/orders/postOrders.ts.
- Tests that drive the store: `_resetOrderBasketStore` and `orderBasketStore.setState(...)` packages/esm-patient-medications-app/src/components/medications-details-table.test.tsx, packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/orders/postOrders.test.ts, packages/esm-patient-orders-app/src/order-basket-action-button/order-basket-action-button.test.tsx.

*Patient chart store — `patient-chart-global-store`*
- `usePatientChartStore` wraps it in `useStoreWithActions` and returns a `fakeStore` when the input `patientUuid` does not match the stored one packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/store/patient-chart-store.ts; `setPatientChartWorkspaceGroupVisitUuid` calls `setState` directly packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/store/patient-chart-store.ts.
- Hook has 73 references across 31 files. The load-bearing ones:
  - `useStartVisitIfNeeded` reads `visitContext` and `workspaceGroupVisitUuid` and resolves pending prompts from a `useEffect` on them — timing/notification changes from the store change when a visit prompt resolves packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/workspaces.ts, feeding `useLaunchWorkspaceRequiringVisit` used to launch `order-basket` packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/workspaces.ts.
  - `useOptimisticVisitMutations` reads `visitContext`/`mutateVisitContext` packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/visit/visit-mutations.ts.
  - `usePatientChartPatientAndVisit` destructures `setPatient`, `setVisitContext`, `visitContext`, `mutateVisitContext` and gates the whole chart's visit loading on `visitContext?.patient.uuid` packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/patient-chart/patient-chart.resources.ts; it also calls `setPatientChartWorkspaceGroupVisitUuid` packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/patient-chart/patient-chart.resources.ts.
  - Visit UI consumers of `visitContext`/`setVisitContext`: `useDeleteVisit` packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/hooks/useDeleteVisit.tsx, `visit-form.workspace` packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visit-form/visit-form.workspace.tsx, `end-visit-dialog.modal` packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visit-prompt/end-visit-dialog.modal.tsx, `visit-context-switcher.modal` packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visits-widget/visit-context/visit-context-switcher.modal.tsx, `current-visit-summary.extension` packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visits-widget/current-visit-summary.extension.tsx, `visit-context-header.extension` packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visits-widget/visit-context/visit-context-header.extension.tsx, `visit-timeline.component` packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visits-widget/single-visit-details/visit-timeline/visit-timeline.component.tsx, `encounters-table.component` packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/visit/visits-widget/past-visits-components/encounters-table/encounters-table.component.tsx, `encounter-list-tabs.extension` packages/esm-patient-chart-app/src/clinical-views/encounter-list/encounter-list-tabs.extension.tsx.
  - Cross-app reads of `visitContext`: `visit-tag.extension` packages/esm-patient-banner-app/src/banner-tags/visit-tag.extension.tsx, `past-visit-tag.extension` packages/esm-patient-banner-app/src/banner-tags/past-visit-tag.extension.tsx, `immunizations-detailed-summary.component` packages/esm-patient-immunizations-app/src/immunizations/immunizations-detailed-summary.component.tsx, `vitals` `useLaunchWorkspaceRequiringVisit` packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/utils.ts.

*Angular form state — `ampath-form-state`*
- The store is subscribed in `ngOnInit` with `store.subscribe` and `changeState` writes through it packages/esm-form-entry-app/src/app/fe-wrapper/fe-wrapper.component.ts, with the unsubscribe in `ngOnDestroy` packages/esm-form-entry-app/src/app/fe-wrapper/fe-wrapper.component.ts. It passes only a name and initial state, so it is unaffected by `storageType` changes but sensitive to registry/reactivation semantics for that name.

**Indirect, via framework hooks**
Both stores are consumed through `useStoreWithActions` from `@openmrs/esm-framework` packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useStore.ts. If the behaviour change alters store identity, subscription notification, or `setState` semantics, these hooks (and therefore every `usePatientChartStore`/`useOrderBasket` consumer above) are affected too, even though they never call `createGlobalStore` themselves.

**Test mocks that shadow the real implementation**
- The Angular tests mock the whole framework, including a hand-rolled `createGlobalStore` with only `getState`/`setState`/`subscribe` and no registry packages/esm-form-entry-app/src/openmrs-esm-framework.mock.ts. A behaviour change would not be caught here, and this mock could diverge.
- React tests stub `usePatientChartStore` itself, e.g. packages/esm-patient-banner-app/src/banner-tags/visit-tag.test.tsx — also insensitive to the change.

**Not verified / out of scope**
- I did not read the bodies of `useStore`/`createUseStore` packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useStore.ts to confirm exactly how subscription comparison is done, so the precise failure mode for consumers is inferred from the hook signature, not confirmed.
- Non-patient-chart modules in the workspace (esm-core's own `workspace2` and `useVisitContextStore`, which also use `useStoreWithActions` packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useVisitContextStore.ts) were outside the requested scope.
- The patient chart's `esm-form-entry-app` bundle may load its own framework copy; the duplicate-instance detection packages/framework/esm-state/src/state.ts means such a copy would get a separate registry, which I did not verify for this package's build config.
